group.passage:
The Terracotta Army is one of the greatest archaeological discoveries of the twentieth century, yet it was found entirely by chance. In 1974, farmers digging a well in northwestern China [[1]] pieces of a clay figure, and archaeologists soon arrived to see what else lay below the fields. What they found was astonishing. Thousands of life-size soldiers, along with horses and chariots, stood in long rows inside huge underground pits.
The figures were made more than 2,200 years ago and buried near the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor to rule a united China, to guard him in the life he believed would follow death. The sheer [[2]] of the project still amazes researchers, who think it must have required a huge number of workers over many years. No two soldiers appear to be exactly alike, for their faces [[3]] a wide range of expressions, from calm to stern. Their hairstyles and armor also differ according to [[4]], so a general can easily be told apart from an ordinary foot soldier. Some kneel as if ready to shoot, while others stand beside their horses.
When they were first made, the figures were painted in [[5]] shades of red, green, blue, and purple. Today, however, almost all of that paint has disappeared. The colors proved extremely [[6]]: once exposed to the dry air, they began to curl and flake off within minutes. For this reason, archaeologists have [[7]] digging up much of the remaining army until better ways of protecting the paint are developed. They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world. For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.

10.strategy_zh: scholars and the merely ___ alike 要兩群人並列；the ＋形容詞可以指人，想想前一句的遊客是什麼樣的人。
hints: the merely ___ 與 scholars 並列，指一群人。
the ＋形容詞可以表示「…的人」，例如 the rich。
前一句的數百萬遊客，大多是出於什麼心情來參觀？

translation_zh.text:
兵馬俑是二十世紀最偉大的考古發現之一，然而它完全是偶然被發現的。1974年，在中國西北部挖井的農民挖到了一尊陶俑的碎片，考古學家隨即趕來，想看看田地底下還埋著什麼。他們的發現令人驚嘆：數以千計真人大小的士兵，連同馬匹和戰車，在巨大的地下俑坑裡排成長列。
這些陶俑製作於兩千兩百多年前，埋在秦始皇——第一位統治統一中國的皇帝——的陵墓附近，要在他所相信的死後世界裡守護他。這項工程驚人的規模至今仍令研究人員讚嘆，他們認為它必定動用了大量工人、耗費許多年才完成。沒有兩個士兵看起來完全相同，因為他們臉上帶著各式各樣的表情，從平靜到嚴肅都有。他們的髮型和盔甲也依階級而不同，所以將軍很容易就能和普通步兵區分開來。有些跪著，彷彿隨時準備射擊；有些則站在戰馬旁。
這些陶俑剛完成時，塗著鮮豔的紅、綠、藍、紫色。然而如今，那些顏料幾乎都已消失。這些色彩極為脆弱：一接觸乾燥的空氣，幾分鐘內就開始捲曲、剝落。因此，考古學家暫緩挖掘大部分尚未出土的軍隊，直到研發出更好的顏料保護方法為止。他們也一直沒有開啟秦始皇本人的墓室，希望讓它保持完整，直到能在不造成損壞的情況下研究它。
自從遺址開放參觀以來，已吸引了來自世界各地的數百萬名遊客。無論是學者還是純粹出於好奇的人，這支沉默的軍隊都提供了一個難得的機會，讓人與古代世界面對面。

evidence: In 1974, farmers digging a well in northwestern China [[1]] pieces of a clay figure, and archaeologists soon arrived to see what else lay below the fields.
yet it was found entirely by chance
1.explanation_zh: turned up pieces of a clay figure＝挖到、發現陶俑碎片，與 found entirely by chance 呼應。

evidence: The sheer [[2]] of the project still amazes researchers, who think it must have required a huge number of workers over many years.
it must have required a huge number of workers over many years
2.explanation_zh: the sheer scale of the project＝工程規模之大，後文說需要大量工人與多年時間。

evidence: No two soldiers appear to be exactly alike, for their faces [[3]] a wide range of expressions, from calm to stern.
3.explanation_zh: faces wore a wide range of expressions＝臉上帶著各種表情；wear an expression 為固定搭配。

evidence: Their hairstyles and armor also differ according to [[4]], so a general can easily be told apart from an ordinary foot soldier.
so a general can easily be told apart from an ordinary foot soldier
4.explanation_zh: differ according to rank＝依階級而不同，後文說將軍與步兵一眼可分。

evidence: When they were first made, the figures were painted in [[5]] shades of red, green, blue, and purple.
5.explanation_zh: vivid shades of red, green, blue, and purple＝鮮豔的色彩，與如今顏料幾乎消失對比。

evidence: The colors proved extremely [[6]]: once exposed to the dry air, they began to curl and flake off within minutes.
they began to curl and flake off within minutes
6.explanation_zh: proved extremely fragile＝極易損壞，冒號後說接觸乾燥空氣幾分鐘內就捲曲剝落。

evidence: For this reason, archaeologists have [[7]] digging up much of the remaining army until better ways of protecting the paint are developed.
7.explanation_zh: have held off digging up＝暫緩挖掘，until better ways ... are developed 支持。

evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
8.explanation_zh: keep it intact＝保持完整，與 without causing damage 呼應。

evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
9.explanation_zh: it has drawn millions of visitors＝吸引數百萬遊客；現在完成式需過去分詞。

evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
10.explanation_zh: the merely curious＝只是好奇的人（the＋形容詞表一群人），與 scholars 對照。

evidence: In 1974, farmers digging a well in northwestern China [[1]] pieces of a clay figure, and archaeologists soon arrived to see what else lay below the fields.
1.explanation_zh: 首句說是偶然發現，農夫挖井時意外發現陶俑碎片，turned up 表示（偶然）發現。

evidence: The sheer [[2]] of the project still amazes researchers, who think it must have required a huge number of workers over many years.
2.explanation_zh: the sheer scale of the project：工程規模龐大，需要大量工人，scale 最合。

evidence: No two soldiers appear to be exactly alike, for their faces [[3]] a wide range of expressions, from calm to stern.
3.explanation_zh: wear an expression 指臉上帶著表情，wore a wide range of expressions。

evidence: Their hairstyles and armor also differ according to [[4]], so a general can easily be told apart from an ordinary foot soldier.
4.explanation_zh: 後面說將軍與一般步兵能區分，髮型與盔甲依軍階（rank）而不同。

evidence: When they were first made, the figures were painted in [[5]] shades of red, green, blue, and purple.
5.explanation_zh: 紅綠藍紫等色調，vivid 指鮮豔，並與後文顏料剝落形成對比。

6.explanation_zh: 冒號後說明一接觸乾燥空氣就捲曲剝落，表示顏料極易損壞，fragile 最合。

7.explanation_zh: have held off + V-ing 表示暫緩，until 之後說等到有保護顏料的方法。

8.explanation_zh: left ... unopened，希望保持其完好無損，keep it intact。

9.explanation_zh: has drawn millions of visitors：吸引數百萬遊客。

10.explanation_zh: scholars 與 the merely curious 對照，指只是好奇的一般人。

H.explanation_zh: rank（名詞，階級）不合：空格在 have ___ digging up 中，需要過去分詞，後接動名詞。

I.evidence: For this reason, archaeologists have [[7]] digging up much of the remaining army until better ways of protecting the paint are developed.
I.explanation_zh: turn up 不接動名詞，「找到挖掘」不通，也與 until… 的「等到…才」不合。

J.evidence: For this reason, archaeologists have [[7]] digging up much of the remaining army until better ways of protecting the paint are developed.
J.explanation_zh: fragile（形容詞，脆弱的）不合：空格在 have ___ digging up 中，需要過去分詞，後接動名詞。

B.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
B.explanation_zh: keep it drawn（keep＋受詞＋過去分詞）形式上可以，但「使墓室保持被吸引／被拉開」不通；句尾 without causing damage 要的是完整無損。

C.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
C.explanation_zh: wore（動詞過去式，穿戴；面帶）不合：空格在 keep it ___ 中（keep＋受詞＋形容詞），需要形容詞。

D.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
D.explanation_zh: 受詞是尚未開啟的墓室，keep it vivid 不通；句尾 without causing damage 要的是完整無損。

E.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
E.explanation_zh: scale（名詞，規模）不合：空格在 keep it ___ 中（keep＋受詞＋形容詞），需要形容詞。

F.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
F.explanation_zh: keep it held off（使墓室保持被擋開）不通；句尾 without causing damage 要的是完整無損。

G.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.

H.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
H.explanation_zh: rank（名詞，階級）不合：空格在 keep it ___ 中（keep＋受詞＋形容詞），需要形容詞。

I.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
I.explanation_zh: keep it turned up（使墓室保持調高／被挖出）與「不開啟墓室」矛盾。

J.evidence: They have also left the emperor’s own burial chamber unopened, hoping to keep it [[8]] until it can be studied without causing damage.
J.explanation_zh: 希望墓室「保持脆弱」不合邏輯。

A.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.

C.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
C.explanation_zh: wore 是過去式，不能放在 has 後面。

D.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
D.explanation_zh: vivid（形容詞，鮮豔的）不合：空格在 it has ___ millions of visitors 中，需要及物動詞的過去分詞。

E.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
E.explanation_zh: scale（名詞，規模）不合：空格在 it has ___ millions of visitors 中，需要及物動詞的過去分詞。

F.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
F.explanation_zh: 「擋住」數百萬遊客與句首 Since the site opened to the public 矛盾。

G.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
G.explanation_zh: curious（形容詞，好奇的）不合：空格在 it has ___ millions of visitors 中，需要及物動詞的過去分詞。

H.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
H.explanation_zh: rank（名詞，階級）不合：空格在 it has ___ millions of visitors 中，需要及物動詞的過去分詞。

I.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
I.explanation_zh: turn up 作「出現」時不及物，作「找到」時 it has turned up millions of visitors 語意不通。

J.evidence: Since the site opened to the public, it has [[9]] millions of visitors from around the world.
J.explanation_zh: fragile（形容詞，脆弱的）不合：空格在 it has ___ millions of visitors 中，需要及物動詞的過去分詞。

A.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
A.explanation_zh: the merely intact（只是完整無損的人）不通。

B.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
B.explanation_zh: the merely drawn（只是被吸引的人？）不是英文說法；the＋形容詞指人時要用表示人的特質的形容詞，前一句的遊客是出於好奇而來。

C.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
C.explanation_zh: wore（動詞過去式，穿戴；面帶）不合：空格在 scholars and the merely ___ alike 中，與 scholars 並列指一群人，需要 the＋形容詞（指人）。

D.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
D.explanation_zh: the merely vivid（只是鮮豔的人）不通；vivid 形容顏色、印象，不形容參觀者。

E.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
E.explanation_zh: scale 是名詞，不能放在副詞 merely 後面與 scholars 並列。

F.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
F.explanation_zh: held off（片語動詞過去式／過去分詞，暫緩）不合：空格在 scholars and the merely ___ alike 中，與 scholars 並列指一群人，需要 the＋形容詞（指人）。

H.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
H.explanation_zh: rank 是名詞，the merely rank 不合語法。

I.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
I.explanation_zh: turned up（片語動詞過去式／過去分詞，挖到）不合：空格在 scholars and the merely ___ alike 中，與 scholars 並列指一群人，需要 the＋形容詞（指人）。

J.evidence: For scholars and the merely [[10]] alike, the silent army offers a rare chance to stand face to face with the ancient world.
J.explanation_zh: the merely fragile（只是脆弱的人）與參觀遊客無關。
